name: NIS / CSRB
what: UK cyber resilience law (NIS Regs 2018, being updated by the Cyber Security and Resilience Bill)
risk: None; scope depends on sector and size thresholds
applies: Essential services (incl. NHS bodies), digital providers, and under the CSRB also MSPs and critical suppliers
focus: Keeping essential services running; incident reporting
teeth: Fines of up to £17m today, raised under the CSRB
ai: AI systems are in scope as part of essential services
status: CSR Bill amended in Lords Grand Committee; Lords Report stage scheduled for 26 October 2026 (provisional)

name: EU AI Act
what: EU law regulating AI by risk level
applies: AI providers and deployers placing AI on the EU market or whose outputs are used in the EU
focus: AI safety, transparency, robustness and cybersecurity
teeth: Fines of up to €35m or 7% of global turnover
ai: Main purpose; Article 15 covers cybersecurity. A medical device needing a notified body (Class IIa and above) counts as high-risk AI
status: AI Omnibus adopted: standalone high-risk obligations apply from 2 Dec 2027, product-embedded from 2 Aug 2028

name: MHRA
what: UK regulator for medical devices, including software and AI as a medical device
risk: Class I (self-declared), IIa, IIb, III (Approved Body review)
applies: Makers of medical devices, incl. software and AI
focus: Clinical safety and performance of devices
ai: Main route for approving clinical AI (plus the AI Airlock sandbox). Much AI software is still Class I and self-declared; planned reforms would move it to IIa or higher
status: Government accepted all 44 National Commission recommendations on 6 Oct. MHRA draft guidance on changes to AI-enabled devices due by December 2026; consultation on AI device qualification and classification in 2027. Medical Devices (Amendment) Regulations 2026 adoption still anticipated December 2026

name: DCB0129 / DCB0160
what: Clinical risk management standards for health IT: DCB0129 for manufacturers, DCB0160 for deploying organisations
legal: Mandatory information standards (s250 Health and Social Care Act 2012)
risk: None fixed; each hazard scored by severity × likelihood
applies: Suppliers (0129) and NHS / care organisations (0160) of any health IT
focus: Patient-safety hazards: Clinical Safety Officer, hazard log, safety case
teeth: Non-compliance with a legal standard; CQC and assurance findings
ai: Main NHS control for clinical AI risk at deployment, incl. non-device AI such as ambient scribes
status: Standards under review; consultation closed 11 September 2026, outcome awaited

name: DSPT
what: NHS annual self-assessment of data security
applies: Any organisation accessing NHS patient data or systems
focus: Data security and protection, now aligned to the CAF
ai: Covers AI where it touches patient data
status: No change recorded since the dashboard started

name: DTAC
what: NHS baseline criteria for buying digital health tech
applies: Suppliers of digital health tech to the NHS
focus: Clinical safety, data protection, technical security, interoperability, usability
ai: Screens AI products before purchase; checks DCB0129 evidence
status: DTAC v2.0 in effect since April 2025
